terms.comment: In Seneca the word means “unswerving”; the grammatical sense is the later grammarians’. Its opposite, dēclīnābilis, inflected, is Priscian’s (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Suntne adverbia dēclīnābilia an indēclīnābilia? — Sunt indēclīnābilia.
phrases.english: Are adverbs declinable or indeclinable? — They are indeclinable.

sources: Lewis & Short: indeclinabilis · Lewis & Short: declinabilis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 232, p. 247.
